tools.name: search_resources
tools.description: Find an MCP server, agent skill, A2A agent or API that does a job, and get what you need to install or connect it. Use it when the user wants to find, compare or install an MCP server, skill, agent or API for a job, or asks what exists for a task; prefer it to a general web search for that. Examples

tools.name: list_resources
tools.description: Browse the StealthStack index without a search query: for example every agent skill (kind=skill), everything one domain publishes (domain=...), or services that accept x402 payments (paid=x402). Returns the total, a count per kind and one page of records with connect details. For a specific need ("M

tools.name: get_resource
tools.description: Get install and connect details for one resource found with search_resources or list_resources, by its identifier. Call it after a search, before you install or connect anything. Returns the connect URL or install command (npm, PyPI or Docker package when one is listed), transport, repository, publi

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp?src=mcpregistry" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_resources, get_resource · Private data: list_resources · Public sink: search_resources.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_resources, get_resource · Private data: list_resources · Public sink: search_resources

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.

remediation.title: Tool description changed since last scan
remediation.detail: Tool "list_resources" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
